independent.summary: The safety net doesn't actually withhold the question: chat.js passes `reason: question` — the same string it pushes into `pendingQuestions` — and `buildHandoffSms`/`buildHandoffEmail` print it verbatim as `Visitor needs help: "<reason>"` / `Reason: <reason>` one line above the filtered block, and `lastMessage` (usually the same visitor text) is printed too, so a matched question is still relayed in full in both SMS and email; the test named 'buildQuestionBlock omits a matched question from the alert body' only exercises `buildQuestionBlock`, never the assembled body, so it cannot catch this.

`sendHandoffFollowUpNotification` still calls `buildQuestionBlock(pendingQuestions, SMS_QUESTION_CAP)` and `buildQuestionBlock(pendingQuestions)` with no `doNotRelay` argument, so a question suppressed in the initial alert reappears unfiltered in every follow-up reminder SMS/email (up to `handoffFollowUp.maxReminders`).

"Don't relay this type" puts visitor-authored text (the pending question, verbatim) onto the list, and `buildSystemPrompt` interpolates list entries straight into the system prompt; `sanitizeList` only trims/caps/dedupes and neutralises nothing, so a visitor who crafts a question containing instruction-like text gets it injected into the prompt as soon as an owner clicks the one-click button.

grades.reason: The PATCH handler this button calls runs `sanitizeDoNotRelay` on write (dashboard.js, `if ('doNotRelay' in updates)`), so the claim of "no validation or sanitization" is untrue, and the finding names no concrete failure that client-side sanitising would prevent.
